findings.rationale: Public activation uses a route-local response helper with no-store, request-ID, and noindex headers; this route predates authenticated session helpers and has a dedicated activation boundary guard.
Public activation must read the raw body to enforce declared and actual UTF-8 byte limits before JSON parsing; its dedicated guard verifies this exact ordering.
The secret-authenticated cron route uses a route-local response helper because it conditionally adds Retry-After and request-ID headers while preserving no-store behavior.
Public signup uses a route-local response helper with no-store, request-ID, and noindex headers plus a deliberately minimal accepted response that avoids account-existence disclosure.
Public signup reads the raw body to enforce declared and actual UTF-8 byte limits before JSON parsing; its dedicated public-signup guard verifies this ordering.
The intentionally minimal public status endpoint has no authentication context and returns only service/environment/git metadata with no-store and noindex headers.
